fable.meaning: a short story with a moral, often with talking animals

faced.meaning: having a particular kind of face; confronted with (past of face)

facet.meaning: a distinct feature or element in a problem
facet.example: he studied every facet of the question

faint.meaning: weak or dim; to lose consciousness briefly

fairy.meaning: a small being, human in form, playful and having magical powers

faith.meaning: a strong belief in a supernatural power or powers that control human destiny
faith.example: he lost his faith but not his morality

false.meaning: not in accordance with the fact or reality or actuality

fancy.meaning: elaborate or expensive; to like or want

farce.meaning: a comedy characterized by broad satire and improbable situations

fault.meaning: a mistake or flaw; responsibility for a problem

favor.meaning: a kind act done for someone; to prefer

feast.meaning: a ceremonial dinner party for many people

feign.meaning: make believe with the intent to deceive
feign.example: He feigned that he was ill

felon.meaning: someone who has committed a crime or has been legally convicted of a crime

femur.meaning: the longest and thickest bone of the human skeleton

fence.meaning: a barrier that serves to enclose an area

feral.meaning: wild, especially of a domestic animal gone wild

ferry.meaning: a boat that carries people and cars across water

fetal.meaning: of or relating to a fetus

fetch.meaning: go or come after and bring or take back

fever.meaning: a rise in the temperature of the body

fiber.meaning: a slender and greatly elongated substance capable of being spun into yarn

field.meaning: a piece of land cleared of trees and usually enclosed
field.example: he planted a field of wheat

fifth.meaning: coming next after the fourth and just before the sixth in position

filet.meaning: a boneless steak cut from the tenderloin of beef

filmy.meaning: so thin as to transmit light

final.meaning: occurring at or forming an end or termination

finch.meaning: any of numerous small songbirds with short stout bills adapted for crushing seeds

first.meaning: preceding all others in time or space or degree
first.example: the first house on the right

flair.example: he has a flair for mathematics

flame.meaning: the hot glowing part of a fire

flank.meaning: the side of something, e.g. of a body or army

flare.meaning: a sudden burst of flame or light; a signal light
flare.example: a flare lit up the sky

fleet.meaning: a group of ships or vehicles under one command

flesh.meaning: the soft tissue of the body of a vertebrate: mainly muscle tissue and fat

flick.meaning: a light sharp contact (usually with something flexible)
flick.example: he gave it a flick with his finger

flirt.meaning: talk or behave amorously, without serious intentions
flirt.example: My husband never flirts with other women

float.meaning: rest on the surface of a liquid or in the air

flock.meaning: a group of birds or sheep

flood.meaning: an overflow of water onto normally dry land

floor.meaning: the inside lower horizontal surface (as of a room, hallway, tent, or other structure)
floor.example: they needed rugs to cover the bare floors

flora.meaning: all the plant life in a particular region or period

floss.meaning: thin thread for cleaning between teeth

flour.meaning: fine powdery foodstuff obtained by grinding and sifting the meal of a cereal grain

fluid.meaning: a substance that is fluid at room temperature and pressure

flung.meaning: past tense of fling: threw with force

flush.meaning: go red in the face; wash out with a rush of water

foamy.meaning: full of or covered with foam

focal.meaning: having or localized centrally at a focus

focus.meaning: the concentration of attention or energy on something
focus.example: the focus of activity shifted to molecular biology

foist.example: He foisted his work on me

folly.meaning: the trait of acting stupidly or rashly

force.meaning: to cause to do through pressure or necessity, by physical, moral or intellectual means
force.example: She forced him to take a job in the city

forge.meaning: shape metal by heating and hammering; fake a signature

forgo.meaning: do without or cease to hold or adhere to

forum.meaning: a public meeting or assembly for open discussion

found.meaning: set up an organisation; past tense of find

frame.meaning: a border for a picture; a basic structure

frank.meaning: characterized by directness in manner or speech
frank.example: tell me what you think--and you may just as well be frank

fraud.meaning: intentional deception resulting in injury to another person

freak.meaning: someone obsessed with something; a very unusual event

frill.meaning: a decorative ruffle on clothes; an extra

frisk.meaning: the act of searching someone for concealed weapons or illegal drugs
frisk.example: he gave the suspect a quick frisk

frizz.meaning: the condition of being formed into small tight curls
frizz.example: her hair was in a frizz

frond.meaning: compound leaf of a fern or palm or cycad

front.meaning: the side that is forward or prominent

frost.meaning: ice crystals forming a white deposit (especially on objects outside)

froth.meaning: a mass of small bubbles formed in or on a liquid

frown.meaning: look angry or sullen, wrinkle one's forehead, as if to signal disapproval

froze.meaning: past tense of freeze: turned to ice, or stopped still

fruit.meaning: the ripened reproductive body of a seed plant

fully.meaning: to the greatest degree or extent

fungi.meaning: plural of fungus: mushrooms, moulds and yeasts

funny.example: funny stories that made everybody laugh

furor.meaning: an outbreak of public anger or excitement

fussy.meaning: hard to please; too concerned with details

fuzzy.meaning: covered in soft fine hair; blurry
